astronomy_picture_of_the_day.title: Uranus's Largest Moon: Titania
astronomy_picture_of_the_day.explanation: Titania's tortured terrain is a mix of canyons, cliffs, and craters.  NASA's interplanetary robot spacecraft Voyager 2 passed the largest moon of Uranus in 1986 and took the feature picture. That the trenches of Titania resemble those on another moon of Uranus, Ariel, indicate that Titania underwent some violent surface event possibly related to water freezing and expanding in its distant past.
